intro: Castlemorton is a parish under the southern end of the Malvern Hills in Worcestershire. Beside Hancocks Lane leans a native black poplar, its massive trunk tipped over the verge and crowned with a fan of straight young stems, which a reader photographed and sent to us. They give it about 250 years and a girth of three metres; we would like to know its history.

trees.story:
A reader sent us this tree from Hancocks Lane at Castlemorton, under the southern end of the Malvern Hills, with a GPS fix taken at the trunk and its name written out in full: Populus nigra subsp. betulifolia, the native black poplar. They give it about 250 years and a girth of 300 centimetres; those figures are theirs.

The tree has done most of its living at an angle. The massive trunk leans hard out over the dry grass beside the lane, its bark dark and ridged, and then stops at a swollen knuckle at about head height. From there a whole fan of straight young stems shoots upward, the look of a tree that was once pollarded, cut back to its head for poles, and has kept regrowing ever since. In the reader's photograph a man stands beside it with one arm raised to the head of the trunk, and only just reaches.

We do not know who cut it last, or what the lane remembers of it. If you do, tell us here and we will add your words to the page.

Look at it from the lane first, then from the low side of the lean.
